name: Müller and Bostrom expert survey (2012-2013)
role_summary: Questionnaire of four groups of AI experts run Nov 2012 to May 2013 by Vincent C. Müller and Nick Bostrom (Future of Humanity Institute, Oxford); published 2014
inclusion_note: Earliest widely cited expert survey giving years for a 10/50/90% chance of human-level machine intelligence; the reference point from before the deep-learning boom.

name: AI Impacts Expert Survey on Progress in AI (Grace et al.)
role_summary: Repeated survey of authors at top machine learning conferences run by AI Impacts (2016, 2022, 2023); papers by Grace et al.
inclusion_note: The largest repeated survey of machine learning researchers on when machines will outdo humans at all tasks; same core question across three waves allows a trend.

name: Metaculus
role_summary: Online forecasting platform where registered users submit probability forecasts that are pooled into a community prediction (not a money market)
inclusion_note: Its question on when the first general AI system will be announced (question 5121) is the most cited public crowd forecast of AGI timing; no readings could be retrieved in this session (see search_log).

name: Manifold Markets
role_summary: Play-money prediction market where traders buy and sell shares on questions; prices read as probabilities
inclusion_note: Public API exposes every trade with timestamps so a market's probability can be read at any past date; its AGI markets have hundreds of traders.

name: Pew Research Center
role_summary: Nonpartisan U.S. research organisation; runs the American Trends Panel, a probability-based online/phone panel of U.S. adults
inclusion_note: Anchor for U.S. public mood: the same 'more concerned than excited about AI in daily life' question asked 2021-2025 on a probability sample

name: YouGov
role_summary: Online polling firm; U.S. opt-in panel weighted to census targets; runs daily single-question surveys and longer topical polls
inclusion_note: Anchor for public views closest to AGI: repeated questions on AI ending the human race (2023-2026) and on AI becoming more intelligent than people (2023-2024)

name: Monmouth University Polling Institute
role_summary: University polling institute in New Jersey; national random-sample telephone polls of U.S. adults
inclusion_note: Anchor for the earliest repeated public question on AI as a threat to the human race: identical wording asked in 2015 and 2023

name: Ipsos
role_summary: Global market research firm; Global Advisor online surveys across about 30 countries (Ipsos AI Monitor series)
inclusion_note: Anchor for cross-national public feeling: the repeated 'AI products make me nervous / excited' statements, 28-32 country averages 2021-2025, plus a 2019 worry item

name: Google Trends
role_summary: Google's public tool showing relative search interest (0-100 index) for terms and topics over time and place
inclusion_note: Anchor for public attention: worldwide relative search interest in AGI, superintelligence and singularity terms, 2005-2026

name: Geoffrey Hinton
role_summary: Computer scientist and deep learning pioneer; University of Toronto professor (emeritus); co-founded DNNresearch 2012 (bought by Google 2013); Google VP and Engineering Fellow 2013-2023 (staff role, did not lead the company); left Google 2023 to speak about AI risk; Turing Award 2018, Nobel Prize in Physics 2024
inclusion_note: earliest hinton-2015-01 (2015-05, said at the Royal Society machine learning conference, reported in The New Yorker 2015-11-16); latest hinton-2026-01 (2026-09-16, congressional briefing, secondhand). Fixed year-by-year web searches ran for 2005-2015 only; the search budget ran out before 2016-2026, which were covered by fetching known sources.

name: Sam Altman
role_summary: OpenAI co-founder 2015 and co-chair 2015-2019; CEO 2019-present (removed 2023-11-17, reinstated 2023-11-21 to 22 per Wikipedia, Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI); president of Y Combinator 2014-2019; co-founded Loopt 2005

name: Ray Kurzweil
role_summary: Inventor and futurist; author of The Singularity Is Near (2005), How to Create a Mind (2012) and The Singularity Is Nearer (2024); Director of Engineering at Google from December 2012 (an employee, not a company leader)
inclusion_note: earliest kurzweil-2005-01 (2005-09); latest kurzweil-2026-01 (2026-01). Fixed queries run for every year 2005-2026.

name: Gary Marcus
role_summary: Cognitive scientist, NYU professor (emeritus); author of Kluge (2008), Rebooting AI (2019, with Ernest Davis) and Taming Silicon Valley (2024); founder of Geometric Intelligence (2014-2016, sold to Uber) and Robust.AI (2019); writes the Marcus on AI newsletter (2022-present); testified to the US Senate 2023. Never led a frontier model lab.
inclusion_note: earliest marcus-2012-01 (2012-11-24); latest marcus-2026-08 (2026-09-10). Fixed yearly searches run for every year 2005-2026; newsletter 2022-2026 sampled by keyword.

name: Yann LeCun
role_summary: Computer scientist and NYU professor; founding director of Facebook AI Research about 2013-2018 and Meta Chief AI Scientist about 2018-2025 (his own post: 12 years at Meta, 5 as FAIR founding director, 7 as Chief AI Scientist); left Meta at the end of 2025 to found the Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI) world-model startup, 2026-present
